notes:
A television no longer loses the room without asking, and music no longer starts at whisper volume when it takes one over.

IT ASKS BEFORE TAKING THE ROOM. When a television is playing through a Sonos and you send music to that room, Sorriva now stops and says so - "Living Room is actively playing TV audio" - with Cancel and Play. Press Cancel and nothing reaches the speaker; press Play and the music goes on as before. It covers every way audio can arrive in a room: playing an album or a station, playing from Apple Music, moving what is playing from another room, and adding the room to a group that is already playing.

IT ONLY ASKS WHEN SOMEONE IS ACTUALLY WATCHING. This is the part that took the measuring. Sonos keeps a room on its TV input for HOURS after the set is switched off, so a warning based on "is this room on the television" would appear all evening, every evening, and you would learn to tap through it. Sorriva asks Sonos a second question - is sound actually coming out of that room - and only warns when the answer is yes. Checked against the whole house with the television on: one room out of thirteen raised it, and the other soundbar, which was not on its TV input, stayed quiet.

MUSIC NO LONGER STARTS ALMOST INAUDIBLE. A soundbar sits at whatever volume the television left it at, which is not a music level - measured at 6 straight after a film, against 12 in the rooms playing music. Take the room for music and the first track would start barely audible. Sorriva now sets the room to a proper starting volume before the music begins. Only that room changes: if it is part of a group, the balance you set across the other rooms is left alone.

AND YOU CHOOSE THE NUMBER. Settings now has a real Playback screen, where the Zones and Playback rows had been greyed-out placeholders. It carries a switch to turn the behaviour off entirely and a slider for the starting volume, set to 7 out of the box.

A BUG YOU COULD NOT HAVE SEEN. The app had quietly stopped compiling - not from anything anyone wrote, but from a change underneath it in Apple's tools. It had been that way for some time before anything tried to build. Fixed, and worth noting that the one-second test suite cannot catch this kind of break at all; only building the app finds it.

ALSO. Build times were remeasured and the project notes corrected: an ordinary edit-and-run is under ten seconds, not the twenty previously recorded.

NOT IN THIS RELEASE. The starting volume is one number for the whole house. An Arc Ultra and an Era 100 do not sound the same at 7, so a second television in another room would want its own setting. Remembering what each room was last playing music at is the better answer and is not built.
